title: Government's Procurement of Goods and Services during COVID-19 Pandemic
what_it_is: Government's Procurement of Goods and Services during COVID-19 Pandemic

sections.label: COVID-19 government procurement framework
sections.summary: The question asks about the framework for COVID-19 procurement, GeBIZ proportion, considerations for other contracts, and enterprise participation, while limited tenders or direct contracting are permitted under specific conditions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) what has been the framework for Government's procurement of goods and services to address the COVID-19 pandemic; (b) what proportion of such contracts, by dollar value, have been issued through the standard Government procurement system on GeBIZ; (c) what are the considerations when issuing contracts otherwise; and (d) what steps are taken to ensure that all enterprises can participate in such procurement opportunities so as to ensure provision at competitive prices and quality.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: However, the use of limited tenders or direct contracting is permitted under specific conditions, such as to protect public health, or for reasons of national security.

sections.label: Emergency Procurement direct contracting
sections.summary: Emergency Procurement allows agencies to directly contract with suppliers outside GeBIZ, as done for premises for at-risk persons and essential medical supplies.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: For such instances, the procedures under Emergency Procurement allow Government agencies to directly contract with suppliers who have the necessary expertise and resources, instead of going through open sourcing.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: For example, as we needed to quickly source for and fit out premises to house at-risk persons, and also secure essential medical supplies, the agencies concerned established direct contracts with the suppliers outside GeBIZ who were best able to meet the requirements within the shortest timeframe possible.

sections.label: GeBIZ proportion and audit reviews
sections.summary: The COVID-19 procurement proportion through GeBIZ is not yet available, more procurement will use GeBIZ as urgency lessens, direct contracts require reasonable quotes, and transactions face audit and compliance reviews.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The proportion of COVID-19 related procurement by dollar value through GeBIZ as compared with other modes is not yet available, as such procurement is still on-going.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: As the situation improves and there is less time urgency, a larger proportion of procurement will be carried out through the default process of open sourcing via GeBIZ.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: In the event that direct contracting is used, Government agencies are still expected to assess that the quotes from the suppliers are reasonable, by comparing against prevailing market benchmarks and taking into account the time constraints and world-wide market situation.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: As with all procurements, transactions done during this period are subject to audit and compliance reviews by relevant authorities.

sections.label: Audit and disclosure framework compliance
sections.summary: All this remains subject to audit and compliance reviews, and the disclosure framework will be complied with in due course.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And it is important to remember that all this is still subject to audit and compliance reviews.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, the framework for disclosure that we have in place will be complied with in due course.
